questions.text: In the lm() summary output, what does the 'Std. Error' column represent?
options: The residual standard deviation of the response variable
The standard deviation of the estimated coefficient across repeated samples
The absolute value of the residuals
The standard deviation of the predictor variable x
questions.explanation: The standard error of a coefficient measures how precisely it is estimated — it is the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of that coefficient. Smaller Std. Error = more precise estimate.

questions.text: An lm() summary shows R-squared = 0.86. What does this mean?
options: 86% of observations lie within one standard deviation of the fitted line
The model makes correct predictions 86% of the time
86% of the variance in y is explained by the predictor(s) in the model
There is an 86% probability that the model is correctly specified
questions.explanation: R-squared is the proportion of variance in the response (y) explained by the model. R² = 0.86 means the predictor(s) account for 86% of the variation in y; the remaining 14% is unexplained (residual).

questions.text: lm() uses an iterative algorithm and therefore requires starting values, just like optim().
questions.explanation: lm() uses QR decomposition — a direct (non-iterative) algorithm that computes the exact solution in one pass. No starting values are needed.

options: A vector of fitted values for each observation
Confidence intervals for the fitted values at each observed x
Confidence intervals for the model coefficients (intercept and slope)
A hypothesis test for the overall model fit
questions.explanation: confint() computes confidence intervals for each coefficient (by default, 95%). These are the intervals within which the true parameter values are expected to fall with the stated confidence level.

questions.text: The p-value for the slope in an lm() summary is 0.0001. This tells you that:
options: There is a 0.01% chance that x causes y
If the true slope were zero, observing a slope this large or larger purely by chance has probability 0.0001
The model explains 99.99% of the variance in y
questions.explanation: A p-value is the probability of observing a test statistic as extreme as the one computed, assuming the null hypothesis (β=0) is true. Small p-values indicate that the null hypothesis is unlikely given the data.
